Purpose: Reduced lineages of this family in environmental or uncultured settings
Query string: ("genome reduction" OR "genome streamlining" OR "reduced genome" OR "streamlined genome" OR "genome degeneration") AND (Mycobacterium OR Mycolicibacterium OR Mycobacteriaceae OR mycobacteria OR Corynebacteriales) AND (freshwater OR environmental OR uncultured OR "metagenome-assembled" OR lake OR oligotroph)

Purpose: Reduced lineages of this family irrespective of habitat
Query string: ("genome reduction" OR "genome streamlining" OR "reduced genome" OR "streamlined genome" OR "genome degeneration") AND (Mycobacterium OR Mycolicibacterium OR Mycobacteriaceae OR mycobacteria OR Corynebacteriales)

Purpose: Reduced freshwater lineages in any phylum
Query string: ("genome reduction" OR "genome streamlining" OR "reduced genome" OR "streamlined genome" OR "genome degeneration") AND (freshwater OR environmental OR uncultured OR "metagenome-assembled" OR lake OR oligotroph)

Purpose: PubMed, Europe PMC, Google Scholar, bioRxiv
Query string: Searched 7 September 2026. No date, language or publication-type limit. Title/abstract/keyword fields where the interface supports field restriction, all fields otherwise.

Purpose: Single-pass on title and abstract, full text where the abstract was ambiguous
Query string: Retained if a bacterial lineage with a reduced genome was described. Screening question: is any lineage within the Mycobacteriaceae both reduced and not host-associated? Excluded: records reporting no reduced lineage, and method or resource papers without a lineage description.

Purpose: No coherent reduced Mycobacteriaceae lineage outside host association was found
Query string: Reduced Mycobacteriaceae recovered were all host-associated (M. leprae, M. lepromatosis, M. uberis, M. ulcerans, M. lepraemurium, M. shottsii). Reduced freshwater lineages recovered were all in other phyla and are listed row by row in S26a.

Purpose: Targeted search, not a systematic review
Query string: Per-record counts at each screening stage were not retained, and no citation chasing was performed beyond the records returned by the queries. PubMed, Europe PMC and bioRxiv return stable result sets for a fixed query, and therefore runs 1-3 can be repeated there exactly; Google Scholar ranks and personalises results and does not; it was used only to widen coverage and no claim depends on it alone.
